chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abu al-Husayn al-Tamimi from Safwan from Yazid ibn Khalifa said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was with him. A man said to him: 'My servant threw a basket in my house, and inside it were two eggs from the birds of the Sanctuary (Haram).' He (AS) said: 'Upon him is the value of the two eggs; he feeds it to the birds of the Sanctuary. And the value of the two eggs and the value of the bird are equal.'

key_terms.حَمَامُ الْحَرَمِ: Sacred birds of the Sanctuary (specifically pigeons/doves in Mecca)
key_terms.يَعْلِفُ بِهِ: He feeds it with it (referring to the compensation value)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for accidentally killing a sacred bird in the Haram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the compensation for accidentally killing a sacred bird of the Haram is determined by the bird's value, which is equated to the value of its eggs, ensuring the penalty is proportional to the loss. This ruling highlights the sanctity of the Haram's ecosystem and the practical application of kaffarah, where the compensation is specifically designated to feed the remaining sacred birds, reinforcing the continuity of their care. The hadith underscores the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding accidental transgressions by pilgrims, distinguishing between the value of the creature and its offspring while maintaining the economic and spiritual integrity of the holy site.
